name: Nilus Scholasticus
bio: Nilus Scholasticus is one of the named epigrammatists of the Greek Anthology. Paton’s Index of Authors gives no date for him; the title Scholasticus (a lawyer or man of letters) is common among the poets of the sixth century.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 247.

poems.title: Book XVI, 247: On a Satyr in Mosaic at Antioch
poems.author: Nilus Scholasticus
poems.text: A. All Satyrs are fond of jeering, but tell me, thou too, why, looking at everyone, dost thou pour forth this laughter? B. I laugh because I marvel how, being put together out of all kinds of stones, I suddenly became a Satyr.
